extraction.method: Opened each complete PDF with fitz; extracted every page with Page.get_text('text') and explicit PDF page markers. All sources use sort=True except the two Whitney Newey MIT PDFs, re-extracted with sort=False for readable slide order. No OCR or web snippets were used.
extraction.scope: All pages of all nine PDFs were extracted. Reading status below is separately limited to the stated complete focused texts or selected units.

sources.title: Nonparametric Regression: Nearest Neighbors and Kernels
sources.author: Ryan Tibshirani
sources.edition: Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning lecture notes, Spring 2024; complete 11-page PDF
sources.authority: University of California, Berkeley, Department of Statistics, instructor-hosted course notes
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 1-11; extracted lines 1-586; §§1-3.6 and references, especially §§2.3-2.4 and 3.1-3.6. Figures were not visually inspected.
sources.anchors_and_limits: kNN universal-consistency statement and Lipschitz risk sketch (§2); Nadaraya-Watson definition and risk calculations (§3); local-linear weighted least squares and moment cancellation (§3.5-3.6). Universal consistency cites Györfi et al.; the minimax claim is asserted/deferred; some design and boundary hypotheses are described only as mild. Use as a focused source for estimator definitions and proof routes, not as a self-sufficient proof of every rate.

sources.title: Nonparametric Regression: Splines and RKHS Methods
sources.author: Ryan Tibshirani
sources.edition: Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning lecture notes, Spring 2023; complete 21-page PDF
sources.authority: University of California, Berkeley, Department of Statistics, instructor-hosted course notes
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 1-21; extracted lines 1-1171; §§1-5.4 and references. Figures were not visually inspected.
sources.anchors_and_limits: Cubic smoothing-spline definition and direct orthogonality/representer proof (§2.2-2.4); natural boundary conditions and linear-smoother form. The written existence/rank step for a natural interpolant is only a dimension-count assertion; for one distinct input the claimed uniqueness fails. Higher-order risk rates are asserted without proof, the RKHS representer theorem is left as an exercise, and some Sobolev/B-spline details are deferred. Use the cubic proof only after adding at least two distinct design points and closing interpolation existence/full rank.

sources.title: Semiparametric theory
sources.author: Edward H. Kennedy
sources.authority: Author paper hosted by arXiv; author affiliated with Carnegie Mellon University Department of Statistics
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 1-8; extracted lines 1-343; §§1-5 and references, especially §§3-4.
sources.anchors_and_limits: Estimator asymptotic linearity and estimator influence function (§3); DQM paths, scores, tangent and nuisance-tangent spaces, pathwise derivatives, influence curves and efficient projection (§4). The paper identifies itself as a brief review and does not prove the general regularity, closure, Riesz, or lower-bound results. Its causal running example is not a proposed category-1 dependency.

sources.title: B-Splines and Spline Approximation
sources.author: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers
sources.edition: CIME 2017 course notes; complete 39-page author/institution-hosted PDF
sources.authority: Authors' university departments: University of Oslo and University of Rome Tor Vergata; hosted on Speleers' institutional mathematics site
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 1-39; extracted lines 1-1697; §§1.1-1.4 and 2.1-2.3, including all displayed supporting proofs.
sources.anchors_and_limits: B-spline recurrence, support, smoothness, nonnegativity, partition of unity, Marsden identity and spline-space basis results in §1; bounded local quasi-interpolant error Theorem 32; best-approximation Theorem 41 and existence construction Theorem 48 in §2.3. The proof of uniform constants for arbitrary knots uses a thinning argument whose detailed construction is not included. Prefer Theorem 32 for an explicitly bounded local quasi-interpolant and uniform or controlled local mesh; do not use the stronger arbitrary-knot constant without adding that proof.

sources.title: Nonparametric and Semiparametric Estimation
sources.author: Whitney K. Newey
sources.edition: MIT 14.385 Nonlinear Econometric Analysis course notes, Fall 2007; complete 24-page PDF
sources.authority: MIT OpenCourseWare, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 1-24; extracted lines 1-1589; all pages. The final sort=False extraction was re-read completely after its line count was reconciled.
sources.anchors_and_limits: KDE construction and bias derivation/proposition (pp. 1-5); variance and pointwise MSE (pp. 3-5); integrated and multivariate rates (pp. 5-7); Nadaraya-Watson and local-linear definitions/calculations (pp. 8-16); series regression Proposition 3 and complete projection/trace proof (pp. 10-11); partially linear series estimation Proposition 7 and proof (pp. 21-24). Several boundary, smoothness-uniformity, and design matrix conditions are implicit. The series bound controls expected in-sample empirical prediction error and must not be relabelled independent test risk. Slides contain some broken superscripts; displayed algebra and formulas were checked against their rate balance.

sources.title: Semiparametric Models and Estimators
sources.author: Whitney K. Newey
sources.edition: MIT 14.385 Nonlinear Econometric Analysis course slides, October 2007; complete 19-page PDF
sources.authority: MIT OpenCourseWare, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 1-19; extracted lines 1-350; every slide.
sources.anchors_and_limits: Defines semiparametric models and examples, extremum estimators, generic consistency/asymptotic-normality propositions, and profiling in partially linear/index regression. Tangent-space, pathwise derivative and efficient-score geometry are not developed; some propositions are labelled well-known/straightforward rather than proved. Supplementary interface source only.

sources.title: Nonparametric Smoothing
sources.author: Adrian Bowman and Ludger Evers
sources.edition: Academy for PhD Training in Statistics lecture notes, 2013-14 University of Glasgow course copy; complete 103-page PDF extracted
sources.authority: Academy for PhD Training in Statistics and School of Mathematics & Statistics, University of Glasgow
sources.read_status: partial reading of longer notes; every selected unit read completely
sources.actual_reading: PDF pp. 6-14, extracted lines 157-954 (§1.2 density, §1.3 smoothing, §1.4 local regression); PDF pp. 21-24, lines 1264-1530 (§§2.1-2.2 local mean/local linear); PDF pp. 32-52, lines 1918-3481 (§§3.2.1-3.2.4 univariate splines). Other pages were not read. Figures were not visually inspected.
sources.anchors_and_limits: Density KDE bias/variance/MISE and local-regression formulas are informal, with incomplete technical conditions. §3.2.3 gives the integration-by-parts roughness proof. Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 3.5 rely on a dimension-count interpolation argument; footnote 4 explicitly says full rank remains to be proved. The theorem also needs at least two distinct design points for uniqueness. B-spline recursion/properties are introduced, with some proofs assigned as exercises. Independent corroboration, not a sole proof source.

sources.title: Introduction to Empirical Processes and Semiparametric Inference
sources.author: Michael R. Kosorok
sources.edition: Author-hosted preliminary version, August 2006; 289-page file, not a complete published book edition. The file includes the overview and empirical-process chapters, then jumps from Chapter 14 notes to references; advertised Part III Chapters 16-22 are absent.
sources.authority: Author-hosted University of North Carolina website. The title page permits a noncommercial printed copy and expressly prohibits redistribution in print or electronic form; source is held only in the user-authorized private local analysis cache and is not reproduced in the dossier.
sources.read_status: partial reading of preliminary longer text; complete Chapter 3 read
sources.actual_reading: Complete Chapter 3, printed pp. 33-46; physical PDF pp. 42-55; extracted lines 1675-2347. No other chapters were read as mathematical source text.
sources.anchors_and_limits: Chapter 3 defines the model/parameter setup, DQM score paths, tangent set, asymptotic influence functions, pathwise derivatives, efficient influence functions, efficient scores and estimating equations; theorem 3.1 states a plug-in efficient-score asymptotic result and lists conditions (3.6)-(3.8). The chapter says proofs/details are generally deferred to Part III. Do not claim or cite the absent Part III proofs or the absent remainder of the advertised full text.

sources.title: Semiparametric Statistics
sources.author: A. W. van der Vaart
sources.edition: Expanded St-Flour 1999 lecture notes, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1784, Springer, 2002; complete 120-page author/institution-hosted copy
sources.authority: Author affiliated with Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam; PDF hosted on the University of Washington empirical-process working-group site
sources.read_status: partial reading of longer lecture treatise; selected complete lectures/sections read
sources.actual_reading: Lecture 1, printed pp. 6-14, lines 117-537; Lecture 2, pp. 15-25, lines 538-1012; Lecture 3, pp. 26-37, lines 1013-1610; Lecture 4, pp. 38-50, lines 1611-2215; Lecture 6 §§6.5-6.6, pp. 73-78, lines 3253-3510; Lecture 7 §§7.1-7.3, pp. 79-85, lines 3512-3879. All selected units were read in full. Other pages/lectures were not read.
sources.anchors_and_limits: Lecture 1: DQM and proof that scores are mean-zero finite-variance, tangent sets/spaces, pathwise derivative/Riesz representation, tangent information and LAN likelihood expansion Lemma 1.10. Lecture 2: Cramér-Rao lower bounds and efficient-score projections; later theorem proofs partly deferred. Lecture 3: score/information operators, adjoints and pathwise differentiability; conditional-score transformation lemma. Lecture 4: contiguity, Le Cam lemmas, Gaussian representation and convolution/minimax results; Le Cam's first-lemma proof is omitted. Lecture 6 Theorem 6.29 proves nuisance Z-estimator asymptotic normality under DQM, nonsingular derivative, no-bias and L2 conditions, and a fixed Donsker class with square-integrable envelope; Lecture 7 Theorem 7.2 applies it to efficient-score equations. The preface explicitly says a number of proofs are omitted; record those gaps and the exact selected reading.

cautions: Full extraction is not claimed as full reading for the three longer works.
The natural-cubic interpolation full-rank step is not closed by the two lecture-note dimension-count arguments; proposed scaffold must prove it under distinct-knot hypotheses.
No source supplies fully stated boundary/uniformity hypotheses for every kernel regression claim; the proposed result items must state and prove only conditions they verify.
No source-based claim is made that efficient influence curves guarantee an attaining estimator without additional construction and regularity assumptions.
